result.topic_en: Euler lists closed-form reductions of the double sums $\int\frac{1}{z^m}(\frac{1}{y})$ to products of ordinary power sums, first for the case where m+n is odd, then in interpolated form valid for all orders.
result.transcription:
164 MEDITATIONES CIRCA
quae expreſſiones ita ad paritatem numeri $m$ et $n$
ſunt adſtrictae, vt ad impares per interpolationem
transferri nequeant.
Pro ordinibus quibus $m+n$ eſt numerus
impar.
$\int\frac{1}{z^{2}}\left(\frac{1}{y}\right) = 2\int\frac{1}{z^{3}}$
$\int\frac{1}{z^{4}}\left(\frac{1}{y}\right) = 3\int\frac{1}{z^{5}} - \int\frac{1}{z^{2}}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^{3}}$
$\int\frac{1}{z^{6}}\left(\frac{1}{y}\right) = 4\int\frac{1}{z^{7}} - \int\frac{1}{z^{2}}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^{5}} - \int\frac{1}{z^{3}}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^{4}}$
$\int\frac{1}{z^{8}}\left(\frac{1}{y}\right) = 5\int\frac{1}{z^{9}} - \int\frac{1}{z^{2}}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^{7}} - \int\frac{1}{z^{3}}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^{6}} - \int\frac{1}{z^{4}}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^{5}}$
$\int\frac{1}{z^{10}}\left(\frac{1}{y}\right) = 6\int\frac{1}{z^{11}} - \int\frac{1}{z^{2}}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^{9}} - \int\frac{1}{z^{3}}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^{8}} - \int\frac{1}{z^{4}}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^{7}}$
$- \int\frac{1}{z^{5}}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^{6}}$
etc.
Hic autem nihil impedit, quominus hae expreſſio-
nes etiam ad ordines pares transferantur.
22. Interpolatione autem rite inſtituta hae
ſummationes pro omnibus ordinibus ita ſe habebunt:
$2\int\frac{1}{z^{2}}\left(\frac{1}{y}\right) = 4\int\frac{1}{z^{3}}$
$2\int\frac{1}{z^{3}}\left(\frac{1}{y}\right) = 5\int\frac{1}{z^{4}} - \int\frac{1}{z^{2}}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^{2}}$
$2\int\frac{1}{z^{4}}\left(\frac{1}{y}\right) = 6\int\frac{1}{z^{5}} - 2\int\frac{1}{z^{2}}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^{3}}$
$2\int\frac{1}{z^{5}}\left(\frac{1}{y}\right) = 7\int\frac{1}{z^{6}} - 2\int\frac{1}{z^{2}}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^{4}} - \int\frac{1}{z^{3}}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^{3}}$
$2\int\frac{1}{z^{6}}\left(\frac{1}{y}\right) = 8\int\frac{1}{z^{7}} - 2\int\frac{1}{z^{2}}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^{5}} - 2\int\frac{1}{z^{3}}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^{4}}$
$2\int\frac{1}{z^{7}}\left(\frac{1}{y}\right) = 9\int\frac{1}{z^{8}} - 2\int\frac{1}{z^{2}}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^{6}} - 2\int\frac{1}{z^{3}}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^{5}} - \int\frac{1}{z^{4}}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^{4}}$
$2\int\frac{1}{z^{8}}\left(\frac{1}{y}\right) = 10\int\frac{1}{z^{9}} - 2\int\frac{1}{z^{2}}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^{7}} - 2\int\frac{1}{z^{3}}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^{6}} - 2\int\frac{1}{z^{4}}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^{5}}$
$2\int\frac{1}{z^{9}}\left(\frac{1}{y}\right) = 11\int\frac{1}{z^{10}} - 2\int\frac{1}{z^{2}}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^{8}} - 2\int\frac{1}{z^{3}}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^{7}} - 2\int\frac{1}{z^{4}}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^{6}}$
$- \int\frac{1}{z^{5}}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^{5}}$
etc. vnde

items.quote:
quae expreſſiones ita ad paritatem numeri $m$ et $n$
ſunt adſtrictae, vt ad impares per interpolationem
transferri nequeant.
items.english: These expressions are so bound to the parity of the numbers m and n that they cannot be transferred to odd ones by interpolation.

items.quote:
Hic autem nihil impedit, quominus hae expreſſio-
nes etiam ad ordines pares transferantur.
items.english: Here, however, nothing prevents these expressions from also being transferred to the even orders.
